title: Leopold's AI Fund Implodes, OpenAI Slashes Prices, and AI Now Drives Half of GDP Growth
tldr: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI hedge fund fire-sold $10B+ in stock to Citadel after leveraged bets cratered.
OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 prices up to 80% after cutting its own GPU serving costs.
AI infrastructure spend drove over half of Q2 GDP growth, even as headline growth slowed to 1.5%.

tips.heading: Delete stale AI instructions, rebuild from evidence
steps: Turn off your system prompt, skills, hooks, and custom instructions for a real task.
Add an instruction only when the same mistake repeats, then retest before keeping it.
tips.prompt:
Help me run an ablation test on my AI setup.

TASK:
[Describe a real task.]

GUARDRAILS:
[List the rules that cannot be violated.]

EXIT CRITERIA:
[Define exactly what “done” means.]

VERIFICATION:
[Explain how the result can be tested or inspected.]

Start without relying on my existing skills, hooks, memories, or detailed workflow instructions.

Complete the task, record where you struggle, and distinguish one-time mistakes from repeated failure patterns. Recommend a new instruction only when the same failure occurs repeatedly.

For every proposed instruction:
1. Explain the observed failure it fixes.
2. Write the smallest instruction that could fix it.
3. Retest the task with that instruction added.
4. Keep it only if the result measurably improves.

tips.heading: Turn an idea into a working site with Lovable
steps: In ChatGPT, attach a reference screenshot and describe the app idea, scoped to one user journey.
Ask ChatGPT to convert the conversation into requirements and a brand brief (prompt below).
Create a Lovable project with the screenshot and the requirements, then test and refine.
tips.prompt: Turn our conversation into concise feature requirements and a brand brief for Lovable, including colors, feel, and typography.

news.body: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI hedge fund fire-sells $10B+ to Citadel. Situational Awareness, built on leveraged AI-stock bets, unloaded holdings (SK Hynix, Nebius, Micron, CoreWeave) after margin calls. Peak size is disputed: $20B+ (Neuron/FT) vs. $45B (Morning Brew).
news.means: A cautionary tale on leverage — a correct thesis can still get wiped out by financing timing.
news.source: The Neuron, Morning Brew, The Rundown AI

news.body: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 prices up to 80%. Luna input pricing fell 80% to $0.20/million tokens and Terra fell 20%, after OpenAI's own model rewrote its GPU serving code for a 20% cost cut.
news.means: Costs may drop again soon — recheck client proposals against the new pricing.

beyond_ai.body: US GDP growth slows to 1.5% in Q2, but AI infrastructure spending props up the number. Growth missed the 1.8% forecast and fell from 2.1% the prior quarter; more than half of Q2 growth came from AI-related data-center investment, per Stripe's chief economist, even as consumer spending accelerated to 3.2% on tax refunds and a brief dip in gas prices.
beyond_ai.angle: A live data point for any client budgeting conversation about how much of the current economy is genuinely new demand versus AI infrastructure spend, and the Fed is now weighing a possible September rate move.
beyond_ai.starter: How much of our own growth story this year is real new demand versus AI infrastructure spend propping up the topline?

beyond_ai.body: Tim Cook closes out his final earnings call as Apple CEO. Apple beat on iPhone and Mac revenue, but softness in China and services, plus perceptions that Apple is spending less on AI than rivals, sent the stock lower in after-hours trading; John Ternus takes over as CEO on September 1.
beyond_ai.angle: A textbook case of a leadership transition landing at the same moment as market doubts about AI strategy, useful if you're advising a client through a CEO succession of their own.
beyond_ai.starter: If you were advising Apple's board, would you be worried the market is judging Ternus on an AI story he didn't write?

beyond_ai.body: Amazon's cloud unit beats, and Amazon raises its AI capex guidance to $220 billion. AWS reported its fastest sales growth since Q4 2021, sending the stock up 9% after hours; investors shrugged off the higher 2026 AI spending target, up from $200 billion, given the strong cloud results.
beyond_ai.angle: Cloud and AI infrastructure budgets keep climbing at the biggest players, a useful benchmark when a client pushes back on their own rising AI infra line item.
beyond_ai.starter: If Amazon just raised its AI capex guidance again, are we still comfortable with the budget assumptions in our own AI roadmap?

beyond_ai.body: Jersey Mike's goes public, raising about $1 billion in the largest restaurant IPO since 2021. The sandwich chain priced at $23/share on the NYSE under ticker JMKE, just 18 months after Blackstone bought it, though shares closed down about 6% from the IPO price on debut.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you see Jersey Mike's average location does nearly triple Subway's revenue with a fraction of the locations? Says a lot about franchise economics.

beyond_ai.body: UEFA's 55 member nations threaten to boycott FIFA competitions over a private-equity plan. The dispute centers on a proposal, reportedly involving Josh Kushner, to sell equity stakes in FIFA tournaments including the 2030 World Cup to private investors.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Interesting test case for how much pushback outside capital gets when it touches something as symbolic as the World Cup.
